itens.t: US Federal Reserve Holds Key Interest Rate Steady
itens.r: The United States Federal Reserve decided to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged during its latest policy meeting. Officials noted that they are awaiting the accumulation of more economic data before making further moves. Federal Reserve representatives also emphasized that inflation remains a significant concern. Markets reacted cautiously as investors shifted their focus to upcoming corporate earnings reports.
itens.d:
The U.S. Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate steady on Wednesday, according to an announcement from Washington.

The decision maintains the current monetary policy stance as officials continue to monitor economic conditions.

itens.t: Flavio Bolsonaro Declares Himself Rightful Leader of Brazil From US
itens.r: Following his defeat in the recent Brazilian elections, former presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has declared himself the rightful leader of the country from the United States. His controversial statements have drawn sharp criticism and raised concerns among political analysts and officials back home. The Brazilian Workers' Party expressed fears over a potential 'Guaidó effect' regarding his prolonged stay abroad.
itens.d:
Flavio Bolsonaro has declared himself the rightful leader of Brazil while speaking from the United States.

The declaration comes after he experienced a loss in the recent election.

itens.t: Spain Demands Answers Following Deadly High-Speed Train Disaster
itens.r: At least 68 people were killed and over 100 injured after two high-speed trains collided south of Madrid, sparking nationwide outrage. Violent protests erupted in the capital as angry citizens demanded accountability and the immediate resignation of government officials.
itens.d:
At least 68 people have lost their lives and more than 100 others sustained injuries following a tragic collision involving two high-speed trains.

The deadly accident took place south of Madrid, prompting Spain to demand answers.

itens.t: Alphabet Shares Fall After Revenue Miss and Rising AI Costs
itens.r: Google parent company Alphabet reported quarterly revenues that fell short of Wall Street estimates. High expenditures on artificial intelligence infrastructure significantly accelerated the company's cash burn.
itens.d:
Alphabet shares fell about 8 percent in extended trading after Google's parent company missed Wall Street revenue expectations for the third quarter. Total revenue reached $127.6 billion, falling short of the $128.2 billion estimate due to a drop in advertising revenue.

The revenue miss was driven by high artificial intelligence costs that accelerated cash burn, resulting in a negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion. The company reported an operational loss of $7.66 billion in activities related to AI research and development.

itens.t: South Korea, US and Allies Reaffirm Denuclearization Goal for North Korea
itens.r: Representatives from South Korea, the United States, and partner nations met in Washington to discuss security on the peninsula. The coalition strongly reaffirmed their shared goal of complete denuclearization and pledged tighter enforcement of existing international sanctions against Pyongyang.
itens.d:
South Korea, the United States, and other like-minded allies have reaffirmed their shared goal regarding North Korea.

The countries met in Washington on Wednesday to discuss the denuclearization objective.

itens.t: Putin Woos African Leaders at Summit, Positioning Russia Over 'Colonial' West
itens.r: Russian President Vladimir Putin addressed leaders from dozens of African nations during a high-profile summit. He framed Moscow as a superior, non-colonial partner compared to Western nations.
itens.d:
Russian President Vladimir Putin addressed the leaders of dozens of African nations during a summit meeting.

During the event, he positioned Russia as their best partner in contrast to the colonial West.

itens.t: US Imposes Sanctions on North Korean IT Worker Fraud Network
itens.r: The United States Treasury Department announced new sanctions targeting a North Korean network that deploys IT workers abroad to defraud businesses. These clandestine operations are designed to generate revenue for Pyongyang's advanced weapons programs.
itens.d:
The United States imposed sanctions targeting North Korean government-run schemes that utilize IT workers to defraud American businesses. The Treasury Department stated that these operations generate revenue for Pyongyang's weapons programs.

The fraudulent schemes involve North Korean workers securing employment with companies in the United States and other regions. Pyongyang then takes the majority of their wages to fund weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile development.

itens.t: US Military Captures Image of China's Secretive Space Plane
itens.r: The US military released a remarkably clear satellite photograph capturing China's reusable Shenlong space plane docked in orbit. The image offers a rare glimpse into Beijing's classified space capabilities.
itens.d:
A U.S. military intelligence agency released a photograph of China's secretive, reusable Shenlong space plane docked to another spacecraft in orbit. The image was captured in 2024 by Vantor's WorldView 3 satellite from a distance of 56 miles.

The high-resolution space-based photograph reveals new details about the robotic spacecraft, including its open payload bay doors. Observers have previously noted the vehicle releasing other objects while in orbit during its missions.

itens.t: South Korea Fines Google and Apple Over App Store Practices
itens.r: South Korea's media regulator slapped Google and Apple with a combined fine of 63.71 billion won. The tech giants were penalized for unfairly forcing developers to use proprietary in-app payment systems and delaying app reviews.
itens.d:
South Korea's media regulator fined Google and Apple a combined 63.71 billion won on Wednesday for forcing app developers to use their in-app payment systems. The penalties also targeted unfair delays in app reviews under a 2021 law.

The Korea Media and Communications Commission imposed 42.9 billion won on Google and 20.81 billion won on Apple. This concluded a regulatory process that lasted more than three years.

itens.t: Milwaukee Brewers Manager Faces Scrutiny After World Series Setback
itens.r: The Milwaukee Brewers experienced a crucial setback in the Major League Baseball World Series after a dominant postseason run. Manager Pat Murphy faced heavy scrutiny from fans and analysts following strategic decisions that altered the team's momentum.
itens.d:
The Milwaukee Brewers experienced a setback in the World Series after a thrilling extra-inning loss in Game 4. Prior to the defeat, the team had coasted through the postseason with eight straight wins.

Manager Pat Murphy faced scrutiny following the game as the Tampa Bay Rays stayed alive. The loss put the Brewers just three outs away from victory before the Rays rallied.

itens.t: Virgin Galactic Unveils First Next-Gen 'Delta-Class' Space Plane Named Apeiron
itens.r: Virgin Galactic officially revealed its first next-generation Delta-class space vehicle, named Apeiron, following a worldwide public vote. The new spacecraft is designed to significantly increase flight frequencies for future space tourists.
itens.d:
Virgin Galactic has unveiled Apeiron, the first spacecraft in its next-generation Delta-class vehicle line. The name was selected through a public poll featuring thousands of voters across 83 countries.

The space plane was scheduled to fly from its manufacturing facility in Arizona to Spaceport America in New Mexico. It will undergo final preparations and avionics software work before beginning flight tests.

itens.t: Astronomers Discover Mysterious Large Object Beyond Neptune
itens.r: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected a distant icy object orbiting the sun in the outer edges of the solar system. Designated 2026 ED138, the mysterious body is estimated to measure up to 1,500 kilometers wide.
itens.d:
Astronomers discovered a mysterious large object named 2026 ED138 in the frigid depths beyond Neptune using the Vera Rubin Observatory. The icy body is estimated to be between 600 and 1500 kilometers wide.

Scientists believe the object is likely large enough to be shaped into a sphere by its own gravity, making it a dwarf planet candidate. It was found on October 13 by Matthew Holman using search code developed with Kevin Napier.

itens.t: North Korea Showcases Foreign Goods and New Foldable Phone at Trade Fair

itens.d:
North Korea opened its autumn international trade fair featuring goods from across Asia and very few foreign attendees. External Economic Relations Minister Yun Jong Ho launched the event on Monday.

During the exhibition, state media reported the promotion of a new foldable smartphone alongside various foreign products.

itens.t: Microsoft Cloud Growth and Cash Flow Offer Respite From AI Spending Fears

itens.d:
Microsoft's cloud growth and cash flow have offered respite to investors concerned about high artificial intelligence spending.

The financial metrics helped ease fears surrounding the heavy investments being poured into AI technologies.

itens.t: Vietnam Signs Artemis Accords to Join International Space Coalition
itens.r: Vietnam officially became the 78th nation to sign the Artemis Accords, pledging cooperation in peaceful space exploration. The agreement aligns Hanoi with a growing international coalition guided by transparent and responsible lunar guidelines.
itens.d:
Vietnam has signed the Artemis Accords, becoming the 78th nation to join the international coalition dedicated to the peaceful exploration of space. The signing took place during the Vietnam International Digital Week in Ha Long.

Minister of Science and Technology Vu Hai Quan signed the agreement on behalf of the country. U.S. Ambassador Jennifer Wicks and NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson participated in highlighting the expanding technological cooperation.

itens.t: Critical Firmware Flaw Leaves Most Global Servers Vulnerable to Attack
itens.r: Security researchers uncovered a severe code-execution vulnerability in UEFI firmware utilized by major data centers worldwide. The critical flaw allows potential attackers to compromise systems early in the boot process.
itens.d:
A critical firmware flaw in UEFI security systems leaves most global server vendors and data centers vulnerable to potential attacks.

The security vulnerability allows malicious actors to execute code early during the system boot process.

itens.t: Astronomical Picture of the Day Highlights Mutual Occultation of Jovian Moons
itens.r: NASA's latest Astronomy Picture of the Day captures the fascinating mutual occultation of Jupiter's moons Ganymede and Io. Such rare orbital alignments provide astronomers with vital data on the Jovian system's dynamics.
itens.d:
The video highlights a rare mutual occultation between Ganymede and Io, two of Jupiter's Galilean moons, captured on October 20, 2026. The footage shows Ganymede briefly blocking Io from view in the sky.

Such astronomical events occur when one celestial body passes in front of another, requiring Earth's edge-on view during Jupiter's equinox. Additionally, Ganymede casts a shadow on Jupiter's right side during the rare alignment.

itens.t: Liverpool Edges Chelsea on Penalties to Reach League Cup Quarter-Finals
itens.r: Liverpool secured a hard-fought victory over Chelsea in a dramatic penalty shootout following a 1-1 draw at Anfield. The triumph propels the Reds into the quarter-finals of the English League Cup.
itens.d:
O Liverpool avançou às quartas de final da Copa da Liga Inglesa após vencer o Chelsea por 6 a 5 nos pênaltis em Anfield. O tempo regulamentar terminou empatado em 1 a 1, com gols de pênalti convertidos por Cody Gakpo para os Reds e Morgan Rogers para os Blues.

A disputa de penalidades teve diversas cobranças desperdiçadas por ambos os times até que a batida decisiva de Wesley Fofana foi para fora. Com o resultado, o Liverpool eliminou o adversário e aguarda sorteio para definir seu próximo rival na competição.

itens.t: Corinthians Defeats Santa Fe to Reach Women's Copa Libertadores Final
itens.r: Brazilian powerhouse Corinthians mounted a stunning comeback to defeat Colombia's Santa Fe 2-1. The victory secures 'The Mares' a coveted spot in the final of the women's Copa Libertadores.
itens.d:
O Corinthians garantiu vaga na final da Copa Libertadores da América feminina ao vencer o Santa Fe por 2 a 1 de virada no Equador. O time colombiano abriu o placar no primeiro tempo com um gol de Garavito.

As Brabas empataram ainda na primeira etapa com Letícia e viraram a partida no segundo tempo com um gol de Gi Fernandes. Buscando o sétimo título, o Corinthians manteve o aproveitamento de 100% em finais e aguarda o vencedor do confronto entre Cruzeiro e Olimpia.

itens.t: Petrobras Posts Record Petroleum and Gas Production in Third Quarter
itens.r: State-controlled oil giant Petrobras achieved a historic production milestone by averaging 3.51 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. The impressive volume marks an 11.7% increase compared to the same period in the previous year.
itens.d:
A Petrobras bateu recorde de produção de petróleo e gás no terceiro trimestre de 2026 ao alcançar uma média de 3,51 milhões de barris de óleo equivalente por dia. O volume representa um crescimento de 11,7% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior.

O avanço foi impulsionado pelo aumento gradual da produção nas plataformas dos campos de Búzios e Mero. A companhia também destacou o ganho de eficiência operacional e a redução de paradas para manutenção.

itens.t: UN General Assembly Votes to Condemn US Embargo Against Cuba
itens.r: The United Nations General Assembly overwhelmingly passed a resolution condemning the decades-long US economic embargo against Cuba. Washington pointed to a slight increase in abstentions as proof that its diplomatic isolation strategy is gaining ground.
itens.d:
The UN General Assembly has voted to condemn the ongoing United States embargo against Cuba.

The U.S. pointed to an increase in abstentions during the vote as evidence that its push to isolate Cuba is slowly succeeding.

itens.d:
Families living in Sudan's capital are facing severe economic hardship driven by ongoing conflict and rising inflation.

Soaring food prices and shrinking incomes have forced residents to borrow money and skip meals to survive.

itens.t: Viral AI-Generated Images of North Korean Artillery Near Starbucks Debunked

itens.d:
Viral artificial intelligence-generated images and videos depicting North Korean artillery near a Starbucks in Gimpo have been debunked. The fabricated media circulated widely across social media platforms.

According to a report by NK News, the altered footage originated from real photographs previously published by South Korean news outlets like the Yonhap News Agency.

itens.t: Astronomers Unveil Secrets of 'String of Pearls' Supernova Remnant
itens.r: Scientists have published high-resolution observations of a unique celestial remnant known as the 'string of pearls.' The cosmic structure was created by a supernova explosion witnessed by humanity nearly 850 years ago.
itens.d:
Astronomers are studying Pa 30, a dandelion-shaped supernova remnant in the Milky Way left behind by an explosion witnessed about 850 years ago. The remnant contains a rare zombie star at its center.

The cosmic relic formed from a Type Iax supernova where a white dwarf overfed on a companion star without being completely destroyed. Historical documents from 1181 previously recorded the stellar event.

itens.t: Inside Apple's Historic Decision to Introduce a Touchscreen MacBook Pro

Apple has made a historic decision to introduce a new touchscreen MacBook Pro model.

An exclusive early look reveals the device, marking a significant shift for a computer type the company previously stated would never happen.

itens.t: Milwaukee Brewers Star Jackson Chourio Equals Historic World Series Record
itens.r: Outfielder Jackson Chourio made baseball history by matching a legendary hitting record previously held solely by Babe Ruth. His stellar performance through the first four games of the World Series stunned baseball purists.
itens.d:
Milwaukee Brewers star Jackson Chourio tied a historic World Series record by collecting 10 hits through the first four games. He shares the milestone with Babe Ruth, who achieved the feat in 1928.

Despite Chourio's stellar performance, the Brewers lost Game 4 to the Tampa Bay Rays in extra innings. The team will now look to bounce back in Game 5 to secure their first championship.

itens.t: Legendary Sportscaster Ernie Johnson Announces Departure From 'Inside the NBA'

itens.d:
Longtime 'Inside the NBA' host Ernie Johnson announced that he will step away from the program following the 2026-27 NBA season. Johnson cited heart issues, bypass surgery, and a desire to spend more time with his family as reasons for his departure.

Johnson clarified that he is not retiring entirely from broadcasting and will continue working on other projects like March Madness coverage. He reflected fondly on his 37 years hosting the show before deciding it was time to slow down.
